view: The line DLO trades on is operating profit versus the maintained FY26 OP guide, plus the gross-profit/TPV trajectory, not TPV or EPS headlines. My own arithmetic from the company's figures (FY25 GP $402.8M, OP $220M; H1'26 GP $245.8M, OP $116.9M) puts the guide's implied H2 OP at $163.6-174.6M, up 38-47% YoY, while implied H2 GP is only up 18-27%. At mid-guide GP that needs OP/GP of 61-65% and opex of about $47-52M a quarter, against Q2's 50% and $63M and FY25's 55%. Management has promised exactly that step: World Cup marketing gone, the $4.4M one-off gone, no material headcount growth, AI automation. Consensus EPS of $0.22-0.23 (OP around $76-80M on GP around $130-135M) already prices most of it. TPV guide looks conservative: the implied H2 is roughly Q2's run rate doubled, so TPV and GP likely beat again. Q3 FX was benign: BRL averaged 5.14 in Q3'26 against 5.45 in Q3'25, MXN flat. The Brazil shock landed after quarter-end, so it hits Q4 commentary and the 2027 framing, not Q3 numbers. Management already cited FX headwinds when it held the OP guide in August, and the CEO flagged 'more demanding comparisons' into 2027. I see a real chance of a trimmed or low-end OP guide, or a cautious 2027 tone, against a crowded short and a depressed, Brazil-hit price that would rally on a clean OP step-up. The deciding line is not visible before the release, and the inputs I can see point both ways. Consensus has already moved up to the leverage story, so I cannot show the price is behind on either side. Slightly below a coin flip on the margin record; no recommendation.

recommendation.reason: The reaction turns on whether Q3 shows the promised operating leverage (OP/GP up from 50% toward 58-60%) and whether the FY OP guide survives the post-election BRL drop. Consensus EPS of $0.22-0.23 already embeds most of that step, so neither a beat nor a miss is clearly unpriced. Three of four recent prints fell on margin, which tilts me slightly down. A ~10% short base and the relative cheapness after the Brazil shock pull the other way. Nothing reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 operating profit at or above about $80M (OP/GP of 60% or more) with the OP guide reaffirmed or raised despite FX would make a squeeze-driven up move likely. An OP guide cut citing BRL, or GP/TPV below about 0.68%, would make a down move likely.

self_critique: The case for long: consensus may not fully hold the opex drop. Removing World Cup marketing alone could take opex toward $52-55M, which with a GP beat on conservative TPV guidance would give OP above $80M. A ~10% short base and a Brazil-depressed price would then produce a sharp squeeze, much like the +9.4% March print. The case for short: the company missed EPS consensus last quarter, take rate keeps falling faster than mix explains, and a management that already blamed FX for holding the guide now faces an 8% BRL drop in Q4. Both cases are credible, which is why I stay near 50.
